Implying is key, though. All trials care about intent and what the lawsuit is about. Piracy lawsuits have been largely about attributing loss of revenue or financial damages to the one committing the piracy. There are a few things that can be brought up to convince the jury to nullify the trial.

1) Was the defendant's intention to purchase the media if the piracy method was not available?

2) Did the defendant intend to make available the media after the downloading of said media?

The answer to both of those would be "no." So, there would not be any loss in revenue since the defendant had no intention of buying the media in the first place. And there was no financial damages because the defendant would not be in a position to make said media available for redistribution.

Furthermore, to continue off number 1...
